Subject: Renewal: Ornatek reserved pool uplift + tokens/sec SLO wording

Oliver / team,

Thanks again for the time last week — great to see the plans for the product team ramp and the increased inference volume. As discussed, attached is a concise addendum that (1) increases your Reserved Pool by 8 A100-equivalent GPUs (bringing the total to 32), (2) sets a tokens/sec (TPS) baseline and burst allowance, and (3) adds an SLO paragraph + playbook we use for renewals.

Summary highlights: 
- Committed steady-state: 100k tokens/sec sustained (aggregated across the reserved pool)
- Burst window: additional 30k tokens/sec for 5-minute windows up to 12x/day
- SLO: 99.5% availability of committed TPS measured at 1-minute granularity; credits applied for sustained shortfalls per the addendum

Please find the draft addendum attached (ornatek_proposed_slo_addendum_v1.pdf). Two asks on our side:
1) Confirm that the token accounting model aligns to your expected traffic patterns (sustained vs. spiky). We can supply a short traffic ingestion map to help.
2) Is procurement comfortable with the proposed credit table? We made it intentionally straightforward so legal review is faster.

If this looks directionally right, I can route a cleaned DocuSign version for signature and loop in Monica + Karthik for any technical clarifications during legal review.

Best,
Ben

Ben —

Thanks for the draft. Overall we like the direction but legal and engineering have a few asks / redlines attached. High level concerns:

1) Measurement granularity — Our infra team prefers 5-second sampling windows for KPI reporting rather than 1-minute aggregation; 1-minute hides short spikes that cause tail latency issues for customer-facing endpoints.
2) Burst policy — would like clearer language around how simultaneous bursts from multiple teams are handled (do you prorate across tenants or queue?).
3) Credits — we want a lower threshold before credits trigger (propose 99.7% instead of 99.5%) and a larger credit bucket for repeated outages.

I attached a redline (ornatek_redline_slo.docx) with inline comments. Can you route the redline to your SRE/Runtime team for a technical feasibility pass?

Oliver

Team — forwarding Oliver's redline from Ornatek (attached). Two immediate asks:

- Karthik: can you confirm whether 5-second sampling is something we can reasonably publish as a measurement point for TPS availability? Does it add noise to the credit calculation or risk gaming?
- Monica / Vanessa: if we move credits to trigger at 99.7% and increase the credit cap, what does that do to pricing? We should quantify delta and have a fallback compromise (e.g., move to 99.6% with an enhanced playbook).

Quick context: client is expanding to 32 GPU-equivalent reserved pool and will be on a 12-month renewal. They're sensitive to tail behavior because they run low-latency customer features. I think we can get to an agreement with a small credit uplift and clarifying burst semantics.

Thanks — please reply with short bullets so I can iterate quickly.

—Ben

Ben / team — technical read:

- Measurement granularity: we can expose 5-second sampling for metrics (prometheus style) and keep the credit calculation based on a rolling 1-minute availability window to reduce noise. That gives Ornatek the visibility they want while keeping the SLO stable. We should add a short explanation in the addendum that our monitoring emits 5s metrics but credits use 60s aggregation to avoid transient-triggered credits.

- Burst semantics: propose explicit wording that bursts are capacity-limited and routed on a first-fit basis across the reserved pool, with an automatic fallback to the nearest compatible model variant when the pool is saturated. Multi-team simultaneous bursts will be queued up to the configured burst allowance; we can offer a higher burst allotment as part of the uplift for an incremental fee.

- Credits / thresholds: moving to 99.7% materially increases our financial exposure. If Ornatek needs 99.7%, propose a tiered credit schedule: 99.6% => 5% monthly credit, 99.5% => 12% monthly credit, 99.0% => 25% credit, with a max cap. This reduces the delta between 99.5 and 99.7 while limiting tail exposure.

I can draft suggested legal wording for the monitoring paragraph and the burst playbook.

—Karthik

Subject: Re: Renewal: Ornatek reserved pool uplift + tokens/sec SLO wording

Oliver —

Appreciate the detailed review and the redline. We discussed with our SRE and pricing team and propose the following compromise:

1) Measurement: we will publish 5s metrics for transparency; credits are computed on a rolling 60s availability window. Addendum will include a short paragraph clarifying metrics and where engineering dashboards live.

2) Burst handling: explicit language that bursts are allocated from the reserved pool on a first-fit basis and will be queued when capacity is saturated. During sustained saturation we will automatically failover to a pre-agreed model variant with similar latency/quality characteristics. For Ornatek's uplift to 32 GPUs, we will increase the daily burst allowance to 18 windows (from 12) at no additional charge for the first 3 months post-renewal to ease migration spikes.

3) Credits: we can adopt a tiered credit schedule to reduce exposure: 99.7% => 3% credit, 99.6% => 7% credit, 99.5% => 12% credit. Max monthly credit cap = 30% of monthly bill for the reserved pool. This is a middle ground between your ask and our risk posture.

If Ornatek agrees to this wording I will convert to a DocuSign-ready addendum and share the hubspot/DocuSign link. Monica and Karthik will be available for any follow-up questions during legal review.

Regards,
